chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said:

I entered upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so he brought out to me a perfume box containing musk and said: 'Take from this.' So I took something from it and applied it. He said: 'Refine it (apply more) and put some in your chest.' I said: So I took a little from it and put it in my chest. He said to me: 'Refine it.' So I took from it again, and something remained in my hand. He said to me: 'Put it in your chest.' So I did. Then he said: 'Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: No one refuses the prestige except a donkey.' I said: 'What is the meaning of that?' He said: 'The perfume, and the pillow,' and he listed other things.

key_terms.أَصْلِحْ: Refine it / Apply more (literally: make it good/better)
key_terms.لَبَّة: The chest or upper breast area
key_terms.مَخْزَنَة: A small box or container for storing perfume or spices
key_terms.مِسْك: Musk, a highly valued aromatic substance

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith 'No one refuses the prestige except a donkey' regarding perfume and gifts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) and the virtue of accepting gifts, illustrating that rejecting honor is akin to the stubbornness of a donkey. The Imam’s specific instruction to apply musk to the 'labbah' (the hollow of the throat/chest) underscores the cultural significance of scent as a marker of dignity and social grace in early Islamic society. It serves as a practical reminder that accepting such tokens of respect is an act of gratitude and humility, rather than arrogance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Jahm who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> brought out to me a perfume box in which was musk, and said: ‘Take from this’. So I took something from it, and I applied with it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘More, and make it to be in your chest from it’. So I took a little from it and made it to be in my chest. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘More’. So I took from it again, and there remained something from it in my hand. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Make it to be in your chest’. So I did it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No one refuses the prestige except for a donkey’. I said, ‘What is the meaning of that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The perfume, and the pillow and a number of things’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn Jahm who has said the following:

“I once visited abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He took out a container with musk in it and said, ‘Apply it and place in your nostril.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I took a little and applied to my nostrils.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Apply more.’ I then took more from it and something from it remained on my hand. He (the Imam) said, ‘Apply it to your nostril.’ I applied it.’ He (the Imam) said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘No one rejects honor except a donkey.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then asked, what it means?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is perfumes, pillows’, and he (the Imam) counted certain other things.’”
